solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Open with anger first Christmas present

parts.note: an open, candid person is frank
to incense someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: Advice on how to start the gift-giving: open the presents angrily before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like a verb about unwrapping presents but is an adjective, FRANK. 'Anger' is likewise the verb INCENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi brought gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus, the original Christmas gifts.

clue.text: What amnesiacs must do in Shakespeare — Lear, notoriously!

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words Shakespeare, Lear, notoriously

explanation.surface: A literary quip: in Shakespeare, King Lear famously loses his wits and must learn everything again.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Shakespeare', all of 'Lear' and the first letter of 'notoriously'.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have lost their memory have to acquire their knowledge all over again.

clue.text: The Devil's title, commonly?

parts.note: the Devil is commonly called Old Nick; a familiar informal name is what the answer means

explanation.surface: A question about what people usually call Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is a traditional informal name for the Devil, so his title is literally a Nick name.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal, familiar label used in place of a proper name, as Old Nick is for Satan.

clue.text: It means very little to the Greeks, literally

definitions.meaning: 'literally' means as a letter: one of the letters of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Something of no great importance to the Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literally' means 'as a letter': the word is the ninth, smallest Greek letter, and in English a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth Greek letter, also used in English for the smallest possible quantity, a jot.

clue.text: Tories take on major crime cabal

parts.note: CONS is short for Conservatives, the Tory party
piracy, robbery at sea, is a serious crime

explanation.surface: Conservative politicians tackle a powerful organised crime ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crime cabal' reads as one phrase, but 'cabal' alone is the definition; 'take on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a secret group of plotters, and their scheme or the group itself is a plot.

clue.text: Headless horseman is shorter in summer!

indicators.note: with its head taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a knight is a mounted warrior

explanation.surface: A spooky legend: the Headless Horseman, oddly, seems to be shorter in summer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Headless Horseman of Sleepy Hollow is the false trail; 'Headless' just drops the K, silent anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours between dusk and dawn are fewer in summer, when days are long.

clue.text: Gainfully employed in education? Not entirely

indicators.note: the word is not given in full, losing one letter, here the first

parts.note: learning is education or scholarship

explanation.surface: Is someone in teaching truly gainfully employed? Only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the L from the front of LEARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone making money from their work is drawing an income, paid for their labour.

clue.text: Guess it could be filmed at night

definitions.meaning: a wild guess is a stab made without knowledge

definitions.text: it could be filmed at night
definitions.meaning: taken literally, a camera shot taken in darkness, as at night

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a random guess also describes, literally, a piece of film taken after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild guess is an attempt made blind, like firing at an unseen target.

clue.text: Patsy's cattle with a sense of humour?

definitions.meaning: a patsy is a dupe, someone made a figure of fun

definitions.text: cattle with a sense of humour?
definitions.meaning: livestock (stock) that are chuckling, i.e. laughing cattle

explanation.walkthrough: Stock means farm animals, so cattle that laugh are literally laughing stock; the question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A patsy is a gullible victim, an object of ridicule whom others mock.

clue.text: Henry and Hew given fine for being drunk

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: Two men, Henry and Hew, are fined for drunkenness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hew' looks like a second man's name but is the verb, CUT. HALF-CUT is British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-cut is informal British slang for fairly intoxicated.

clue.text: Revolutionary broadcast eg, in an African country

indicators.note: revolving turns the whole string of letters round, end to end

parts.note: to broadcast is to air
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel radio transmission, for example, in some African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns AIR + EG + IN backwards, giving NI-GE-RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African nation, the continent's most populous.

clue.text: Work out marking for hobby on-line

parts.note: to work out at the gym is to train
spotting is marking with spots

explanation.surface: Exercising and marking things as a pastime done online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-line' is not the internet: the hobby is pursued beside the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting locomotive numbers is a pastime carried out on or beside railway tracks.

clue.text: See 12
A most unusual present captures Penny's character

indicators.note: the word most made unusual is rearranged into a new order

parts.note: present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: A rare gift reveals what Penny is really like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most unusual' reads as one phrase, but 'unusual' only shuffles MOST into TMOS. Then HERE captures P to make PHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere of a place is its prevailing mood or feel, its character.

clue.text: Eastern ornaments broken into microscopic units in US

indicators.note: broken ornaments are smashed into pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Oriental decorations shattered into tiny fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In US' points to the American spelling, -ERS rather than British -RES.
explanation.definitionFit: Billionths of a metre, units for measuring things far too small to see, spelt the American way.

clue.text: Mixed fruit starts off unusually green like ivy

indicators.note: the start of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A bowl of fruit, odd-looking and as green as ivy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' is not an anagram signal: the fruit is a hybrid. The definition is apt since this fruit is indeed green.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican citrus fruit that is a cross of grapefruit, orange and tangerine, so a mixed fruit.

clue.text: Glue applied to a tear can be heated

indicators.note: the glue is applied into the tear, placed inside it

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
gum is a glue

explanation.surface: A repair tip: glue on a rip may need heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heated' suggests the glue, but the definition is a quarrel that can turn heated; 'applied to' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A row or quarrel is often heated, i.e. angry and impassioned, so 'can be heated' describes it.

clue.text: Chap leaves American city to become a drifter

indicators.note: the chap departs, so his letters are taken out

parts.note: Hoboken is a city in New Jersey
Ken is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man quits an American city and becomes a wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoboken, New Jersey, minus KEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An American term for a homeless wanderer, a tramp drifting from place to place.

clue.text: Public transport with hot meal and a drink in South Africa

parts.note: a bus is public transport
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
tea is an evening meal in parts of Britain

explanation.surface: A bus ride, a hot meal and a drink while touring South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA works as the meal and, inside the answer, as the drink, a herbal brew such as rooibos.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion made from local shrubs, such as rooibos, popular in South Africa.

clue.text: It's extremely embarrassing to English and Scottish sport

parts.note: curling, sliding stones over ice, originated in Scotland

explanation.surface: A cringe about the English competing at a Scottish game.
explanation.walkthrough: CURLING is the ice game of sliding granite stones towards a target, born in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so awkward it makes your toes clench is cringingly painful to witness.

clue.text: A refusal to follow reason may lead to hell

indicators.note: the refusal comes after the reasoning in the answer

parts.note: to reason is to infer, deduce
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Refusing to listen to reason can be a road to damnation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason' is the verb INFER, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a raging fire, and Dante's name for the place of eternal damnation.

clue.text: Display screens no longer fitted with inkwells

definitions.meaning: computers' main screens, showing icons, are so called
old school desk lids held inkwells; modern ones do not

explanation.walkthrough: The computer term doubles as the flat upper surfaces of desks, which once had inkwells set in.
explanation.definitionFit: The main screen of a computer, the virtual work surface showing icons and windows.

clue.text: Both get right change for pound

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Both people get the right to swap something for a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' is not money but the verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to beat rhythmically, as a heart or a headache does.

clue.text: Having riotous fun with it would be inappropriate

indicators.note: riotous suggests wild disorder, so the letters of fun are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Having boisterous fun with it would be unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riotous' looks like it describes the fun but signals the rearrangement of FUN into UNF; IT then follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsuitable for a role or purpose is not fit for it.

clue.text: Mostly up and about town in Italy

indicators.note: most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: astir means out of bed and moving about

explanation.surface: Up and about, mostly, in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly up' looks like a phrase, but 'up and about' is one unit, ASTIR, losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Piedmont, famous for its sparkling white wine.

clue.text: Senior citizen on a Hebridean Island

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
Tiree is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: An elderly person living on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: TIREE is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner is someone who has left work, typically in old age.

clue.text: Fatty's raciest version

indicators.note: a new version of the word raciest is made by reordering it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fatty' is not a person: it describes stearic acid, a fatty acid. The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stearic acid is a saturated fatty acid found in animal and vegetable fats.

clue.text: The EU for instance is potentially above Britain

indicators.note: the letters could potentially be arranged otherwise, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: The European Union might be seen as ranking over Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The EU' looks political, but here it is simply a shortened form of 'European Union'.
explanation.definitionFit: EU is a shortened form standing for European Union, an example of a contraction of letters.
